label: DEEP-RESEARCH TASK: DATA / PRODUCTIVITY / UTILITY app feasibility in 2026. For EACH of: G

findings.summary:
In 2026 the Data/Productivity/Utility app class splits cleanly into three integration methods, and VenueOS already owns a widget for nearly all of them, so most are S-effort "reuse our iframe/RSS/data widget + a polished per-app config form" wins. (1) PUBLISH-TO-WEB IFRAME apps — Google Slides, Google Sheets, Google Docs, PowerPoint/OneDrive, Canva live-embed, Google Calendar, Google Maps Embed, Spotify — all still work by having the operator paste a "publish to web / embed" URL that we drop into our existing WEBPAGE sandbox iframe; the only nuance is our null-origin sandbox may need per-app allowances (PDF and some Office embeds need a same-origin/allow-scripts relaxation, and Workspace/M365 admins can disable publishing). (2) FEED apps — News/RSS, sports scores, stocks/crypto, currency, weather, transit/flights, CAP public-alerts — need a light backend fetch+cache (our LIVE_DATA/RSS/WEATHER/CHART widgets already exist) because the raw sources are JSON APIs, not embeds; effort M and the real work is a curated provider + token. (3) NATIVE-RENDER utilities — countdown/clock/QR — we can render ourselves with zero external dependency, so they're pure S config forms. The two genuinely painful ones are Power BI (Microsoft now blocks new "Publish to web" embed codes by default in 2026, pushing everyone to authenticated Embedded — L effort) and any "aggregator-only" social/reviews that don't apply here. Biggest ToS traps: Google News scraping, ESPN's undocumented hidden API for sports scores, and Power BI public-embed being deprecated. Google Slides/Sheets/Docs/Calendar/Maps/Canva/Spotify iframe embeds are officially supported and low-risk. OptiSigns and Yodeck both ship almost this exact list as named "apps," which is the bar to clear — and we can beat them because we already have the AI Concierge to auto-detect and auto-configure these from a pasted URL instead of making the operator hunt for embed codes.</summary>

<uxNotes>[
  "OptiSigns and Yodeck both present integrations as a named, icon-tiled 'Apps' grid with per-app landing pages (optisigns.com/apps-list/<app>), grouped loosely by category (Social, News, Weather, Dashboards, File Management, Business Tools). Each tile has a one-line value prop ('Display your Power BI dashboard on any screen'). This named-tile + one-liner pattern is the bar to match.",
  "Yodeck's list is far deeper (~90+ apps) and leans on pre-baked publisher presets: instead of one generic 'RSS' app it ships ~18 named news feeds (BBC RSS, CNN RSS, ESPN RSS, WSJ, Guardian, Bloomberg, Al-Jazeera...). Turning ONE widget (RSS) into many named tiles by pre-filling the URL is a cheap way to look like you have '90 apps' — high perceived value, near-zero build cost.",
  "Both split time/clock into MANY tiles from one primitive: Analog / Digital / Word / World clock + Count Up / Count Down. Same trick — one native widget, several polished presets = several 'apps'.",
  "Dashboards are the most fragmented category and the one where competitors show the most tiles (Power BI, Power BI w/ Service Principal, Tableau, Tableau JWT, Looker Studio, Qlik, Salesforce, Grafana, Airtable, Smartsheet, Monday, Jira...).
